P4b, P0

The evaluator applies the activated frame's declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra. It distinguishes semantic law, observed evidence, inference and decision, and records every assumption whose failure could change the result.
P6

A frame is bound when every material coordinate of the tuple resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition; the binding may be expressed entirely in source-linked prose, and representation cannot create, widen or replace it.
P3, P6

A reference frame F is the tuple (Q evaluation family; B workspace and topology basis; M material-relation manifold; C coordinate and equality law; I invariant set; A authority relation; E admissible evidence and provenance law; X exclusion and prohibited-assumption set; R closed result algebra of ACTIVATION section 3; J invalidation and rechart condition; K actor capability envelope; D optional declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs involving other frames). The tuple specifies the relation; it is not a required schema or runtime carrier. Operationally a frame is an evaluation contract that defines the finite attention scope one evaluation family requires.

The minimal activation binding, in Markdown or any consumer-selected carrier, is headed 'Reference-Frame Activation: <stable activation identity>' and holds: Frame (declaration identity and revision; exact evaluation and closed result algebra); Subject And Basis (exact subject or candidate identity; workspace, authority, dependency, configuration and time basis); Attention Surface (material relations and applicable invariants; exact source and semantic references; explicit exclusions and prohibited assumptions); Actor And Authority (actor and capability envelope; semantic and evaluation authority; operation authority, subject and territory where material; decision, acceptance and publication authority); Evidence And Relations (admissible evidence and acquisition route; dependency, overlap, input, conjunction or translation relations used; expected result consumer and return relation); Stop And Change (invalidation conditions; stop, residual, re-entry and reconfiguration conditions).

The minimal evaluation result is headed 'Frame Evaluation Result' and holds the fields: frame identity and revision; activation identity; evaluation; subject and basis; actor and capability envelope; semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority; admissible evidence; result; inference relation; residual uncertainty; out_of_frame residual (missing relation or capability, owner, reconfiguration pressure); invalidation conditions; consuming decision or conjunction. The out_of_frame residual field is new in this corpus; it carries what ACTIVATION §3 requires an out_of_frame result to name, and reads none for any other result.

The minimal frame declaration is headed 'Frame: <stable local identity>' and has the sections: Evaluation Family (questions, predicates, and closed result algebra); Subject And Basis (workspace boundary, exact identity, version, time and topology coordinates); Material Manifold (entities, variables, relations, states, and interactions); Coordinates And Equality (how positions are distinguished and related); Invariants (applicable governing laws); Authorities (frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority); Evidence (admissible sources, provenance, and exclusions); Capability Envelope (competence, context, access, tools, evaluation or assurance independence, configuration); Boundary And Exclusions (irrelevant material, prohibited assumptions, and out-of-frame conditions); Optional Frame Relations (inputs, outputs, overlaps, conjunctions, or translations actually used); Invalidation And Recharting (changes that stale this frame or its results); Qualification (representative cases, counterexamples, and known residuals). It is sufficient as written in Markdown or any other consumer-selected carrier.

The boundary between out_of_frame and indeterminate is drawn on what the activated frame declares and on what the step did with it. Three cases; the first two name members of the algebra, and the third names none of its own: out_of_frame when the claim requires a material relation or an evaluator capability that the activated frame does not declare. Whether the step exercised anything is irrelevant to this member; the ground is the missing declaration. indeterminate when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the claim. The result names the evidence that would decide, as its residual uncertainty. Where the claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability, out_of_frame and indeterminate each have a lawful ground; the result names the member it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes neither. The first two cases restate RF-012's members.
P5; rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results
A missing, failed or out-of-scope result returns its own member, never satisfied.
A finite actor realises a selected outer contract through steps; each step's selected context fits the actor's envelope; the actor's internal path within a step is its own.
Standing: recovered as a composite; the generic statement is reframed from the graph profile's graph functions.

A step can meet a condition outside its context and cannot report success on one; its result algebra carries indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis as first-class outcomes and its control model names the next move.
Standing: derived.
Definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing; evidence supports a claim on a basis; authority permits or disposes within scope.
Standing: independent. A bounded actor satisfying all else can still take a green label as acceptance.
The actor of one step need not be the actor of the next; a later actor may re-acquire declared sources but not a prior actor's private memory.
A step's output is a candidate until evaluated.
The world is open: a step may meet conditions outside its selected context.
P0 presupposes a selected outcome (P2).
A declared refinement answers a different question, keeps its own vocabulary and declares a total mapping to the core; no refinement adds a core member.
One core algebra of exactly these five members serves every evaluation and every step's stop state.

Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns invalid_basis or requires reactivation. Apparent equality never substitutes for declared coordinate equality.
P3, P1

Every evaluation returns a member of its declared result algebra. A performed evaluation returns a member; an evaluation not performed because a declared capability was not exercised owes the step's stop state, not a member (ACTIVATION §3, third case). The core algebra is defined once, in ACTIVATION §3: satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, with the meanings and the no-coercion rule given there; this member does not define it a second time. An externally owned compatible extension may refine that algebra while preserving explicit indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure; it may neither add a core member nor coerce one to success.
P5

A step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; an observation reproducible from declared sources is re-acquirable, is not a step-produced fact, and is governed by sufficiency, not conservation.

frame_indexes.scope: Declare a frame, activate it on an exact subject and basis, and return a minimal evaluation result with one member of the result algebra (REFERENCE_FRAME section 13, ACTIVATION sections 1 to 3 and 7). Reselected in set-6 under the 100,000-byte limit for F-01 task A.

residuals.detail: The envelope has four dimensions (context, attention, time, capability). The context dimension is measured in bytes before any read; attention, time and capability have no measure or declaration format, and the documents do not say how a step records that the test was performed on those dimensions.

Each independent commitment carries a one-sentence non-entailment argument in its qualification. These are claims of independence with an informal witness each; none is formalised and P4a states none. The accepted C1 realisation argues them at greater length; the standard conserves only the sentence.

symbols.label: Activated frame: one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct

Activation packet: the minimum an actor receives on activation: one activated frame or one declared active frame configuration with its identity, evaluation, subject, relations, authorities, evidence, envelope, exclusions, dependencies and stop conditions

Authority: an identity-bearing permission to operate or to dispose acceptance within a scope; never minted from capability, label or reachability; its kinds are frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority

Basis: the exact state a step, claim, result or evaluation binds: every version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter it; immutable, or moving with a declared way of detecting advancement and a declared reevaluation condition; mixed bases need an explicit composite relation

Closed result: identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual uncertainty and the invalidation conditions; minimal shape REFERENCE_FRAME section 13; available for reuse under an applicability check

Coordinate: the complete local position from which a value, event, decision, observation or action is interpreted (basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence, authority); equal names, values, shapes or apparent positions do not establish coordinate equality, which follows a declared relation

Capability envelope K (envelope B of ACTIVATION section 2): the competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable independence conditions and configuration required to activate a frame; usable by one actor and not another; it can neither waive an invariant nor widen authority
Evaluator: the relation that applies the declared relation between law and evidence

Evidence: the exact observations or artifacts admitted to evaluate a claim on a basis, each with provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; availability inside a frame makes it neither semantic truth nor decision authority
Fit test of the selected context against the envelope

The frame tuple F = (Q evaluation family, B workspace and topology basis, M manifold, C coordinate and equality law, I invariants, A authority relation, E evidence and provenance law, X exclusions and prohibited assumptions, R closed result algebra, J invalidation and rechart condition, K actor capability envelope, D declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs with other frames)

Minimal activation binding: the carrier-neutral content sufficient to bind one declared frame for one evaluation, under the headings Frame; Subject And Basis; Attention Surface; Actor And Authority; Evidence And Relations; Stop And Change
Minimal evaluation result: the fields of the Frame Evaluation Result shape that close one frame evaluation
Minimal frame declaration: the least content that declares a frame, twelve sections from Evaluation Family to Qualification
Outcome U: a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval
P0 Bounded construction
P1 Interpretation
P2 Purpose
P3 Identity
P4a Typed composition
P5 Totality
P6 Justification and authority
falsified: a declared counterexample defeats it
indeterminate: admissible evidence cannot decide it
invalid_basis: the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation
out_of_frame: the evaluation needs an undeclared material relation or capability
satisfied: the declared predicate holds on the exact basis

Reference frame: a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required to perform one declared evaluation family over a stated basis; its components are the frame tuple
Refinement: ambiguity outcome (resolved, carried, escalated, blocked)
Refinement: construction availability (candidate_ready, refused, incomplete, re_entry_requested)
Refinement: disposition (accept, local_repair, re_enter, reject)
Refinement: profile-defined closure decisions
The one core result algebra for every evaluation and stop state
RF-005 Exact basis and coordinates: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-012 Closed results: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
Selected context: the projection of the closure with its recorded boundary seams
Semantic law: what an evaluation means
Step-produced fact: a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; a reproducible observation is not one
